commands.review_summary:
The PR adds queue wait rejection, Gateway propagation, CLI rendering, and tests so same-session CLI lane waits return structured `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` results.

PR surface: Source +246, Tests +249. Total +495 across 13 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main and `v2026.6.11` log lane-wait facts internally, while the Gateway-backed CLI response type and renderer have no structured lane-busy result. I did not rerun the live two-terminal CLI repro in this read-only review.

target.title: [AI-assisted] fix(cli): surface session lane busy exits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #54622.

A same-session `openclaw agent` CLI dispatch can sit behind an active session lane and fail without telling the operator why. The command queue already has lane-wait diagnostics, but the Gateway/CLI path did not surface them as a structured result. This PR makes CLI-triggered lane waits return a deterministic `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` result instead of a silent generic failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the queue ordering model intact and makes the CLI path opt in to terminal busy rejection when it is waiting behind an active same-session lane. It adds typed wait details, a `rejectOnWait` queue hook, an `AgentSessionLaneBusyError` helper, Gateway response propagation, Swift/protocol response model fields, CLI text/JSON rendering, and tests across queue, Gateway, CLI relay, and embedded-runner lane handling.

This refresh also preserves current-main queue timeout cleanup behavior: `taskTimeoutAbortSignal`, `taskTimeoutAbortGraceMs`, `taskTimeoutReleaseSignal`, and matching `QueueEntry` wiring remain carried through so timed-out embedded runs do not keep lanes held longer than intended.

The compatibility repair removes the transient `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` Gateway agent request parameter from the CLI request, strict protocol schema, and generated Swift request model. Gateway now derives CLI-only busy rejection from the existing Gateway client identity or mode. Non-CLI Gateway agent calls remain unopted, and upgraded CLIs no longer send an unknown strict v4 request field to older daemons.

## User Impact

Operators now get a clear session-lane busy message and retry suggestion when a second CLI dispatch targets a session lane that is already busy. JSON-mode callers receive structured `errorCode: "LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED"` details. Non-CLI agent runs and normal successful CLI runs keep the existing behavior.

Mixed-version Gateway-backed CLI calls no longer fail solely because an upgraded CLI sends `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` to an older strict v4 Gateway. Older daemons may still lack the new lane-busy behavior, but they are not rejected for an unknown agent request parameter.

No new dependencies, config, credentials, network surfaces, or queue policy changes are introduced.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof already supplied in this PR before the current-main refresh used a real Gateway service process and two source-entrypoint CLI `agent` processes against a mock provider. It showed:

- before: a second same-session CLI request eventually reached the provider and returned `SECOND_DONE` with no busy stderr;
- after: a second same-session CLI request exited non-zero before a second provider request and printed `Error: session lane busy (...)` plus a retry suggestion;
- long-active proof after the timer fix: the second request returned `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` while active work was still occupying the lane.

Current-main and compatibility-repair proof on a local OpenClawUbuntu PR lane:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agent.ts`: PASS, all matched files use the correct format.
- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts packages/gateway-client/src/client.watchdog.test.ts`: PASS, 3 Vitest shards in 122.03s; Gateway 380 tests, CLI relay 69 tests, protocol/client 60 tests, 509 tests total.
- Source assertion after the repair: `sourceCliLaneBusyRejection` no longer appears in the changed CLI request, protocol schema, Gateway handler, or generated Swift model surfaces. The CLI test also asserts the Gateway request params do not include that request field, while Gateway handler tests verify CLI client identity still opts into `LANE_WAIT_EXCEEDED` and non-CLI clients remain unopted.

Remaining proof gap: the live two-CLI runtime service proof was not rerun after the current-main refresh and compatibility repair. The focused Gateway/CLI/protocol tests cover the repaired code paths, and the previous real Gateway/CLI behavior proof remains the runtime evidence for the user-visible lane-busy output.
